In 1951, an Indian family-owned company set out to build quality  
pigments. By 2025, that aspiration had become a global leader  
in color solutions.
Color touches everyday life, leaving a lasting impact without noise.  
So does true leadership.
After 75 years of legacy, ONE Sudarshan today leads the world  
in color solutions.
We built our name on pioneering spirit. Today, that spirit stands stronger, 
backed by over 270 years of combined innovation, capability, and 
expertise, and the reach of a true global leader.
Our 75-year journey has been building toward this moment: the integration  
that became ONE Sudarshan, fortifying and accelerating our leadership  
through expanded scale.
One culture, one mission, creating lasting value for all our stakeholders.
Guided by our past. Driven by our future. This is how we lead the  
next chapter of the global color story.Contents

Redefining Global Color Leadership  
Through A Unified Legacy
Seventy-five years since its founding as a pigments manufacturer in 
India,Sudarshan Chemical Industries Limited is now one of the world’s leading 
color solutions providers, integrating 270+ years of combined color expertise.
As a premier global color solutions company, we operate 19 manufacturing facilities across 11 countries, 
serving over 4,000 customers in more than 120 countries. Following the acquisition of the Heubach Group in 
March 2025, which had acquired Clariant’s pigments unit in 2022, Sudarshan has solidified its position as a 
global leader with an unrivaled portfolio of nearly 1,600 products and 63 brands. Our most significant structural 
advantage is our manufacturing footprint, spanning five continents. This provides greater proximity to customers, 
strengthens supply chain resilience, and enhances our ability to respond to regional demand with agility.Corporate Overview Key Highlights

75 Years  
Of Bold ProgressOur Journey
Over 75 years, Sudarshan has 
transformed through bold choices, 
resilient execution, and a relentless 
pursuit of excellence, building a 
legacy that continues to power its 
leadership.
1950s:
BUILD THE FOUNDATION
Founded in 1951 by Dr. R.J. Rathi and L.J. Rathi with an initial 
capital of ₹3,40,000, we began as a trusted domestic pioneer 
of inorganic pigments, engineering our own equipment and 
formulating with locally sourced materials.
1960s:
PIONEERING ORGANIC PIGMENTS
We became India’s first manufacturer of organic 
pigments. While our domestic presence solidified through 
key metropolitan sales in Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, and 
Delhi. Our export footprint expanded into Europe and 
Southeast Asia.
1970s:
ROHA PLANT AND PUBLIC LISTING
We commissioned our flagship Roha facility and listed on 
the Bombay Stock Exchange. In this definitive decade, we 
became the world’s third producer of effect pigments and 
India’s first ISO 9001-certified chemical company.1990s:
QUALITY FOCUS
Adopting Total Quality Management (TQM) principles  
laid the structural bedrock for world-class, high- 
efficiency manufacturing standards at our newly  
established Mahad facility.
2000s:
GOING GLOBAL
We launched a state-of-the-art Pune R&D Center alongside 
North American and European subsidiaries. Our safety 
systems earned the British Safety Council’s prestigious Sword 
of Honour, one of the highest standards for workplace health 
and safety globally.
2020s
A NEW ERA OF COLOR LEADERSHIP
This year marks 75 years since Sudarshan’s founding 
in 1951. It is also the year we became ONE Sudarshan. 
In 2025, we acquired the historic Heubach Group, 
including Clariant’s pigments business (tracing back 
to 1806), creating ONE Sudarshan, the world’s most 
comprehensive integrated pigment platform. Moreover, as 
an industry leader with an unrivaled portfolio, we continue 
scaling high-performance capacities and raising global 
sustainability benchmarks.1980s:
TECHNOLOGY LEAP
Partnering with global giants like Japan’s Dainippon Ink 
and Chemicals (DIC), we injected international technology 
into our processes and diversified into agrochemicals and 
environmental engineering.
2010s 
SHARPENING OUR CORE 
We deepened our pigment focus and expanded our 
operations into China, Mexico, and Japan. We made 
significant investment in green energy and secured 
awards such as the Golden Peacock and Great Place to 
Work certifications.
The Roots of Global Pigments 
While we mark 75 years of Sudarshan this year, 
our origin story as ONE Sudarshan began in 
1806 with the founding of Germany’s Goslarer 
Farbenwerke, marking the beginning of the 
Heubach business. In 1863, Theerfarbenfabrik 
Meister, Lucius & Co. was established in 
Hoechst, specializing in coal-tar dyes and 
forming the earliest thread of Clariant’s legacy. 
By 1869, the Hoechst site expanded rapidly, 
laying the structural groundwork for today’s 
Industriepark Hoechst and pioneering large-
scale pigment innovation across Europe.

Building on Legacy  
Leading with Purpose. Message from the Chairman and Managing Director
FY 2026 was the most transformative year in our history. 
This year, we founded something new: ONE Sudarshan. 
It is a different kind of beginning, built not from scratch, 
but from the combined strength of Sudarshan, Heubach 
and Clariant’s pigment legacies coming together as one, 
making us the world’s leading color solutions company.
A Foundation Built on Principles 
Seventy-five years ago, my uncle, Dr. R. J. Rathi, came 
back from the United States with a PhD in Chemical 
Engineering and a vision. He, along with his brothers, 
started Sudarshan’s journey in 1951 in Pune, with a 
meager capital of ₹340,000. Over these three-quarters 
of a century, we have grown from modest beginnings 
into one of the world’s leading names in the pigment 
industry, built on three principles: meritocracy, discipline, 
and financial rigor. These principles have made us the 
most profitable pure-pigment player and the third-
largest producer in the world, and they still run the 
company today.
The Heubach (including Clariant’s former pigments unit) 
acquisition in March 2025 was our first major move 
as inorganic growth. This made us one of the largest 
pigment producers in the world, bringing together over 
270 years of combined color expertise of Sudarshan, 
Heubach, and Clariant’s legacies. Through this combined 
heritage, we are now the founders of many of the 
molecules that define the pigment industry today. This 
legacy is the foundation of resilience that has carried 
us through cycles of change and enabled the bold, 
transformational steps we have taken in recent years. 
We step into our next chapter with confidence on the 
strength of our people, our global manufacturing footprint 
and our broadening product portfolio. We are optimistic 
that the foundation we have laid will translate into 
sustainable, profitable growth and lasting value for all our 
stakeholders in the years ahead.
A Journey Told in Milestones
Founded in Pune in 1951, Sudarshan began as India’s 
trusted name in inorganic pigments.
In 1968, we became India’s first manufacturer of 
organic pigments.
In 1972, we established our Roha plant and soon after 
listed on the stock exchanges in India and became the 
world’s third company to produce effect pigments.
In 1989, we entered a technology partnership with 
Japan’s Dainippon Ink and Chemicals (DIC), marking a 
leap forward in our manufacturing and R&D capability.
Through the 1990s, we inaugurated our Mahad plant 
and earned India’s first ISO 9001 certification in the 
chemical sector.Leading through Scale and ResilienceDear Shareholders,
As I write to you this year, Sudarshan 
Chemical Industries Limited 
(“Sudarshan”, “the Company”) 
completes a remarkable seventy-five 
years — a Diamond Jubilee that is far 
more than a milestone on a calendar. 
Over these seven and a half decades, 
we have grown from a small local 
pigment manufacturer into one of the 
most respected names in the global 
color pigments industry. Our products 
are lending vibrancy to coatings, 
plastics, inks, and cosmetics that 
touch billions of lives each day. 
Two milestones, one moment:  
From 75 Years of Legacy: 
to a New Era of Leadership.
The 2000s were a decade of leap for our global 
ambitions. We built a state-of-the-art R&D and 
Application Center in Pune. In 2007, we established 
Sudarshan Europe B.V., our first overseas presence, 
laying the foundation for subsidiaries across North 
America and Europe — a period also marked by the 
British Safety Council’s Sword of Honour.
From 2010, we expanded further into Asia-Pacific and 
Latin America — including China, Mexico, and Japan — 
while investing in green energy.
Today, the Company through its subsidiaries operates 
19 manufacturing sites across 11 countries in five 
continents. Roha gives us scale, Frankfurt gives us 
specialties, and other sites provide flexibility. We are not 
immune to demand shifts and policy volatility; however, 
our ability to serve customers has never been stronger, 
given our expanded global presence.
We serve over 4,000 customers in more than 120 
countries and across every major industry, with a portfolio 
of more than 1,600 products — one of the widest ranges 
in our industry — supported by a technology team of over 
200 people.
Three legacies came together this year, making the 
building of one shared culture our focus from day one. 
Our values - REAPS: Respect, Entrepreneurship, Agility, 
Passion, and Seva, guide how we work everywhere.19

=== page 9 ===
The defining task of the year was integration, and I want 
to be candid about that journey. When we began, we soon 
realized we were integrating not two companies but three 
legacies, including that of Clariant’s pigment unit.
From day one we faced pressure on profitability. We 
chose to roll back the additional charge introduced 
during insolvency by the administrator, giving due 
consideration to expectations of our customers. Years 
of operating under insolvency had also left a deep silo 
mindset, with each entity having learned to survive on 
its own rather than thinking as one company. Critical 
leadership talent was missing, and reporting systems 
were far from harmonized.
Faced with this, we made a deliberate choice: to put 
customers first. For the first six to nine months, we chose 
not to chase inventory reduction — in fact, we increased 
it where needed — so we could streamline our supply 
chains, deepen technical marketing engagement, and 
improve customer service to win back trust. That trust 
is returning, and I am proud that several customers 
have recognized us with their “Best Supplier of the 
Year” awards.
In parallel, we pursued value-capture initiatives that 
touched virtually every part of the organization, and it is 
this effort that has delivered a positive EBITDA for the 
acquired business. To make our processes more efficient, 
we have also begun bringing several transactional 
activities back to India and have established our Global 
Capability Center in Pune. On system integration, we 
have started SAP integration project (moving from four to 
one integrated system) to deliver fully harmonized system 
landscape in the next year.
This year we also inaugurated a Global Capability 
Center (GCC) in Pune, a centralized hub to streamline 
operations and develop efficient, agile, and future-ready 
operating models.
Last year, we said we would unlock synergies across 
growth, cost, and cash. The value capture plan made 
good progress and enabled us to deliver a Business 
EBITDA of ₹579 Crores for the pigments business.
Innovation and R&D
With 200+ technology experts across 12 global technical 
centers, we are pioneering sustainable pigment solutions 
and accelerating development in high-performance and 
eco-friendly formulations.
Strengthened technical partnerships and close 
collaboration with customers enable us to co-create 
solutions that set new benchmarks in durability, 
efficiency, and sustainability. From coatings and 
plastics to digital inks, home and personal care, we are 
designing the next generation of colorants — smarter, more sustainable, and precisely tailored to tomorrow’s 
performance needs.
Financial Discipline and Performance:  
What FY 2026 Proved
FY 2026 was not an easy year. Revenue from the 
Sudarshan legacy business remained broadly flat. This 
largely reflected a deliberate rationalization of our go-
to-market and distributor strategy, particularly across 
Europe and Latin America, which created a temporary 
blip, while EBITDA saw a modest dip on account of 
integration related costs absorbed during the year. For 
the acquired group, second and third quarters of the 
year were tough, as global customers worked down 
inventories, which impacted revenue in these quarters. 
However, from the fourth quarter of the year, we started 
seeing a normalization of demand and we expect this to 
continue. Focused value-capture initiatives during the 
year delivered a positive EBITDA turnaround.
Our People, Our Strength
Our people are our biggest strength and greatest 
differentiator. Together we are executing our strategy 
and building a global culture. We are integrating three 
workforces and three ways of working into one. We are 
now home to 3,825 people across India, Europe, the 
Americas, Africa, and Asia, brought together under one 
set of values.Community at Our Core
Our foundation in Pune, Roha, and Mahad built a culture 
of operational rigor that still shapes how we measure 
ourselves. Today, with our global presence, we are 
building on that foundation across all our locations.
Seva, selfless service, is a value we have practiced 
from the start. Through SUDHA, our CSR initiative, we 
support the communities around Roha and Mahad, the 
same villages our founders built alongside.
As ONE Sudarshan, we are carrying this forward 
to every location across the globe. Starting close 
to home, in February we inaugurated the Skill 
Development Center in Gujarat, extending the same 
focus on vocational training and local employment to a 
new community.
Our broader work touched over 130,000 lives this year, 
across education, health, women’s empowerment, and 
community development.Sustainability is in Our DNA
We owe the next generation a better foundation than 
the one we inherited. This year, 56% of our purchased 
electricity came from renewable sources, compared to 
50% last year. We cut freshwater consumption by 27.28%, 
recycled 18.4% more water, and diverted 71.3% of our 
waste away from landfill, while our emissions intensity 
kept falling.
We are also expanding our leadership in sustainable color 
technology: zinc-free anticorrosive pigments, certified 
pigments for biodegradable plastics, and NIR-detectable 
blacks for automated recycling. With over 200 technical 
experts, we are building solutions with our customers, not 
just selling them pigments.
The Path Ahead
The next three years will be a period of unlocking 
profitable growth and making ONE Sudarshan the most 
profitable pigment player in the world and the partner of 
choice for our customers.
I would like to thank our investors for their trust, our 
customers, suppliers, and banking partners for their 
continued support, our Board of Directors for their 
guidance, and our employees for their resilience and 
support throughout this journey to build “One Sudarshan.”
Warm regards,
Rajesh Rathi
Chairman and Managing Director

A Stronger Portfolio  
For A Stronger Sudarshan 
Our expanded product portfolio represents one of the most 
comprehensive platforms in the global pigment industry. 
We provide high-performance, sustainable, and regulatory-
compliant solutions that empower our customers to 
innovate across five key segments.
Coatings: Delivering Complete  
Color Solutions
Sudarshan serves as a premier provider of comprehensive 
color solutions for the global coatings industry, reaching 
far beyond standard pigments to offer superior durability, 
sustainability, and aesthetic excellence. Our portfolio 
supports every layer of a coating system, from decorative 
paints to high-end automotive and protective coatings.
Hostaperm®, Sudaperm®, Novoperm®, and 
Hansa®: Organic pigments providing a full spectrum of 
coloristic and performance properties.
Heucodur®: A range of Complex Inorganic Colored 
Pigments (CICPs) offering exceptional heat stability and 
weather resistance.
Colanyl® 100 and Low-VOC Colanyl ® 500 
series: Globally recognized tinting solutions  
for Point-of-Sale (POS) and industrial systems.
Hostatint: Advanced pigment preparations  
developed for sustainability-focused formulations.LEADING BRANDS AND PREPARATIONSPrinting: Versatility and 
Regulatory Expertise
By uniting two global leaders, we now offer an exceptional 
range of organic pigments for the versatile printing 
industry. Our range covers everything from standard 
applications to the demanding fastness and regulatory 
compliance requirements needed for high-quality food 
packaging. We act as a solution provider for evolving 
regulatory challenges, such as offering compliant Red 2 
pigment combinations to replace chemistries like PR 53:1.Biocide-Free Colorants:
Preservative-Free Innovation
Our innovative Colanyl BF series features liquid pastes 
for aqueous systems that enable the development of 
preservative-free formulations. These solutions allow 
customers to formulate decorative paints in compliance 
with stringent environmental standards, such as Eco 
Label, Nordic Swan, and Blue Angel, while offering 
lower energy consumption compared to traditional stir-
in pigments.
Plastics: Engineering a  
Circular Economy
We are committed to supporting the plastics industry’s 
transition to a circular economy through three core pillars:  
 
NIR-Detectable Black Solutions: Enabling 
automated recycling systems to identify and 
sort black plastic articles across packaging and 
automotive applications.
Composting-Compliant Solutions: An expanded 
range of colorants for bioplastics (e.g., PLA and PHA) that 
meet industrial compostability requirements.
Future-Ready Red Solutions: Providing safe, 
compliant alternatives to traditional pigment chemistries 
to meet evolving global regulatory scrutiny.Inorganic Pigments:
Advanced Inorganic Solutions
The merger has consolidated a powerful range 
of inorganic pigments to meet versatile market 
requirements. By combining expertise, we have 
reactivated our CICP innovation pipeline to push  
the boundaries of durability and heat stability.

The Engine

Management Discussion & Analysis
GLOBAL ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
Despite heightened geopolitical tensions and policy uncertainty, the global economy demonstrated remarkable resilience 
in 2025, achieving a 3.4% growth rate. This steady expansion was primarily fueled by robust global trade and a massive 
surge in tech sector investments, particularly in Artificial Intelligence (AI). Growth was further supported by favorable 
financial conditions, a weaker US dollar, and proactive fiscal measures in major economies, including the US and Germany.
Inflation continued to moderate from earlier peaks, although it remained above comfort levels in several economies due 
to tariff actions, supply chain shifts and renewed energy price volatility. 
Ultimately, trade acted as a critical economic engine, marked by record-breaking merchandise goods trade surpluses in 
China, which hit $1.2 Trillion (6% of GDP) in 2025 and a boom in Asian tech exports. Overcoming early-year trade barriers 
and policy shifts, the global economy closed out 2025 with stronger-than-anticipated momentum, as global growth in the 
fourth quarter of 2025 increased to 3.9% on an annualized basis.
Outlook 
The global outlook became more cautious in early 2026 amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, with 
growth projected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026 before recovering modestly to 3.2% in 2027. Against this backdrop, demand 
for pigments is expected to remain supported by resilient end-use industries, although geopolitical uncertainties and 
evolving trade dynamics may continue to influence supply chains and market sentiment.
(Source: IMF)INDIAN ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
India remained one of the world’s fastest-growing major economies in FY 2026, with GDP growth accelerating to 7.7% 
from 7.1% in FY 2025. This was driven by a 7.9% increase in Gross Value Added (GVA), due to strong performance in the 
manufacturing and services sectors. Concurrently, macro stability was bolstered by a sharp drop in food and fuel prices, 
which helped cool headline inflation to an average of 1.7% between April and December 2025.
The Union Budget 2026-27 reinforces this foundation, targeting a 4.3% fiscal deficit while sustaining aggressive public 
investment. Over 350 structural reforms, including GST 2.0 and new Labour Codes, continue to improve the ease of 
doing business.
Outlook 
India is poised to maintain its global growth leadership, with FY 2027 GDP projected to expand between 6.8% and 7.2%, 
depending on oil prices and geopolitical friction. While headline inflation may experience a minor uptick, it is expected 
to remain within the RBI’s 2%–6% target band. Strong macro fundamentals (infrastructure investment, manufacturing 
expansion, and digitalization) should continue to support demand for pigments across paints and coatings, plastics, and 
inks, among others. 
However, external risks remain elevated, with ongoing conflicts in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, alongside evolving 
tariff regimes and trade restrictions which are contributing to volatility in energy prices, commodity costs, and global 
trade flows. As a net importer of crude oil, India remains exposed to these developments. Currency market volatility could 
continue to exert pressure on the Indian rupee and influence inflation and input cost dynamics.
(Sources: Economic Times , PIB, Economic Survey 2025-26 , India Budget 2026-27 )3.40%

GLOBAL PIGMENTS MARKET 
OVERVIEW
The global color pigments market* is expanding steadily, 
with a current size of nearly $8.6 Billion and an expected 
CAGR of 3% over the next few years. Organic pigments are 
widely used across paints and coatings, plastics, textiles, 
printing inks, cosmetics, and automotive, where their high 
color strength, vivid brightness, and lower environmental 
impact offer clear advantages over inorganic alternatives.
Some Key Observations on the Global Pigments Market:
• Market is increasingly consolidated, but not all 
integrations have created more successful companies.
• Geopolitical volatility underlines the importance of global 
manufacturing footprints and truly global partners.
• Future growth is driven by custom solutions and deep 
pigment expertise.*Excludes Black, White, and Metallic Pigments.
(Source: Internal Pigment industry study and various 
market research reports)

BUSINESS OVERVIEW
Founded in 1951, Sudarshan Chemical Industries Limited 
has grown into one of the world’s leading pigment 
manufacturers, backed by over 270 years of combined 
expertise following the Heubach Group acquisition. Today, 
we are the world’s leading pigment and color solutions 
producer, serving diverse industries with a broad portfolio 
of high-performance, sustainable color solutions.
At a group level, we operate 19 manufacturing facilities 
across 11 countries, as our portfolio spans approximately 
1,600 products and 63 brands, catering to applications 
across coatings, plastics, printing inks, digital inks, special 
applications, including cosmetics, home and personal care, 
agriculture, and other segments.
Innovation remains central to our growth strategy. More 
than 200 technology and R&D professionals across global 
innovation centers work closely with customers to develop 
differentiated solutions, including sustainable and high-
performance pigments that address evolving regulatory 
and market requirements.
Underpinning these capabilities is a strong culture 
of operational excellence, customer-centricity, and 
responsible growth. Guided by the philosophy of Seva, 
Sudarshan combines global capabilities with local 
responsiveness to build enduring customer relationships 
and create long-term stakeholder value.
19 Manufacturing Facilities
11 Countries
1,600+ Products
63 Brands
Through our Subsidiaries we operate 19 manufacturing 
sites across 11 countries and five continents. Roha gives 
us scale and Frankfurt and other German sites handle 
complex specialties. We are not immune to demand shifts 
and policy volatility, but our ability to serve customers 
has never been stronger than before, given our expanded 
global presence.
We serve over 4,000 customers in more than 120 countries 
and across every major industry, with a portfolio of 
more than 1,600 products - one of the widest ranges in 
our industry - supported by a technology team of over 
200 people.
Performance and Integration Review
Comparability between FY 2026 and FY 2025 is 
significantly affected by the first full year of consolidation of the acquired business. Consolidated revenue from 
operations increased to I 9,787 Crores from I 3,346 
Crores. Consolidated EBITDA, excluding other income, was 
I 590 Crores compared with I 381 Crores in the previous 
year. Consolidated profit before tax was I 157 Crores and 
profit after tax was I  41 Crores.
Within the combined pigments business, operating 
conditions were uneven during the year. Revenue in the 
legacy Sudarshan business remained broadly stable, with 
performance influenced by changes to the go-to-market 
and distributor model in parts of Europe and Latin America. 
The acquired business experienced customer destocking 
during parts of the year. Against this background, we 
prioritized customer service, supply reliability, commercial 
and technical support, and value-capture measures 
across procurement, operations and support functions. 
These actions supported an improvement in the operating 
profitability of the acquired business as the year progressed 
and strengthened the platform for future growth.
Integration advanced across commercial, operational, 
technology and support workstreams. ONE Sudarshan 
is migrating from four SAP environments to a common 
platform, expanding shared capabilities and continuing 
to align teams around a common operating model. The 
integration is creating opportunities to simplify processes, 
share expertise, improve visibility across the business and 
use the expanded footprint more effectively. The progress 
achieved during the year provides a stronger foundation 
for further value capture, faster decision-making and more 
consistent customer service.
RIECO Industries Limited also improved performance. The 
business reported revenue of approximately I 268 Crores, 
compared with I 228 Crores in FY 2025, and EBITDA of I 10 
Crores, compared with an EBITDA loss of I 17 Crores in the 
previous year. Management attributed the improvement in 
performance to stronger project execution, organizational 
restructuring, fixed-cost actions and closer project-
cost control.
Balance-sheet focus remained an important priority. 
Net debt stood at I 755 Crores as at 31st March 2026, 
with a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.3x. During the fourth 
quarter, inventory in the acquired business was reduced by  
I 29 Million against an internal target of I 20 Million. We 
will continue to pursue working-capital efficiency while 
maintaining the inventory and service levels required to 
support customers. Financial Performance

RISKS AND CONCERNS 
1. Risk Framework and Assessment 
  Sudarshan operates across diverse geographies, 
exposing itself to a broad spectrum of risks, which 
are proactively monitored, assessed, and mitigated 
through a comprehensive Enterprise Risk Management 
(ERM) framework. 
  This framework is designed to identify uncertainties 
within the business environment and implement 
effective mitigation strategies to address them. 
Sudarshan recognizes potential risks stemming from various sources, including industry-specific 
challenges, sustainability concerns, operational 
disruptions, financial exposures, and cyber \
information security threats. Effective risk 
management and the agility to seize emerging 
opportunities are integral to its strategic approach. 
Risk assessments are conducted by evaluating both 
the potential impact and the likelihood of occurrence 
over various time horizons. 
  The ERM team actively monitors current and emerging 
risks that could influence the achievement of 
strategic and operational objectives. This structured 
risk management approach is closely aligned with 
Sudarshan’s values and forms a core component of its 
overall business model, reinforcing its sustainability. 
2. Risk Management 
  Sudarshan’s risk management framework is overseen 
by the Board of Directors, with dedicated supervision 
by the Risk Management Committee, established in 
accordance with Regulation 21 of the SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015. The primary mandate of the Committee is to 
review its risk management strategy and ensure that 
key risks are effectively managed within defined risk 
tolerance levels.
  The risk management system comprises a formalised 
Risk Management Policy and a dynamic Risk Register, 
both of which are regularly reviewed and updated in 
response to changes in the operating environment and 
business activities. To ensure robustness, independent 
assessments of Sudarshan’s risk management 
controls and procedures are conducted annually.

risk preparedness.

INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEMS AND 
THEIR ADEQUACY 
At Sudarshan, we view internal control as a core pillar of 
corporate governance: one that empowers management 
with operational freedom while maintaining a strict 
framework of checks and balances. We have established a 
robust internal control framework tailored to scale, nature, 
and risk profile to prevent any disruption to our strategic 
objectives. This system provides reasonable assurance 
that all operational transactions are properly authorized, 
accurately recorded, and transparently reported.
To safeguard financial reporting, we utilize a 
comprehensive control framework consisting of entity-
level policies, structured processes, and operating-
level Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Advanced 
Information Technology (IT) policies and systems act as 
critical enablers in this setup. By continuously integrating 
best-in-class automation, refined business processes, and 
the latest digital tools, we consistently reinforce financial 
and commercial discipline.Our integrated control framework is specifically 
engineered to guarantee data credibility and regulatory 
compliance, ensuring:
• Accurate recording and reporting of financial and 
operational information
• Strict adherence to all applicable statutory requirements 
and corporate policies
• Safeguarding corporate assets against unauthorized use 
or disposal
• Executing business transactions strictly within 
approved limits
• Proactive prevention and timely detection of fraud 
and errors
• Continuous modernization and upgrading of core 
IT systems
Management evaluated the effectiveness of our internal 
financial controls over financial reporting as of 31st March 
2026. To ensure an objective and rigorous evaluation, 
Sudarshan appointed Price waterhouse Coopers (PwC) 
to assess these internal controls. Operating under an 
internal audit plan designed in consultation with the Audit 
Committee, their independent assessment confirmed that 
the controls are both adequate and commensurate with the 
scale of our operations.
Following a thorough review of the reports submitted by 
both Management and the Internal Auditors, the Audit 
Committee evaluated the framework in accordance with 
Section 177 of the Companies Act, 2013, and Regulation 
18 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015. Based on this 
evaluation, the Audit Committee concluded that, as of  
31st March 2026, our internal financial controls were 
robust, adequate, and operating effectively.
ENVIRONMENT, SOCIAL, AND 
GOVERNANCE (ESG)
At Sudarshan, we integrate Environmental, Social, and 
Governance (ESG) principles into our business strategy, 
operations, and decision-making, supporting responsible 
growth and long-term value creation.
During FY 2026, the share of renewable electricity in our 
total purchased energy rose to 56%, from 50% the previous 
year, supporting our decarbonisation efforts. We continued 
to strengthen resource efficiency through circular economy 
practices, achieving a 71.3% landfill diversion rate and 
reducing freshwater consumption by 27.28%, supported 
by an 18.4% increase in recycled water usage.We also advanced diversity and workplace safety. Women 
represented 24% of our permanent workforce during 
the year.
A Process Safety Management (PSM) framework, 
introduced across all global sites this year with internal 
audits now underway, and ISO 45001-certified 
manufacturing sites reinforce our focus on employee 
safety. Oversight by a Board-level ESG Committee, led 
by Independent Directors, ensures ESG priorities remain 
embedded across the business, strengthening resilience 
and long-term value creation.Cautionary Statement

16.  RISK MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL:
  The Company has put in place appropriate risk 
assessment and minimisation procedures, which are 
reviewed by the Risk Management Committee, Audit 
Committee and the Board. As per the requirements of 
SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015, a Risk Management 
Committee has been constituted with responsibility 
of preparation of Risk Management Plan, reviewing 
and monitoring the same on regular basis, to identify 
and review critical risks on regular basis, to report key 
changes in critical risks to the Board on an ongoing 
basis, to report critical risks to Audit Committee in 
detail on yearly basis and such other functions as 
may be prescribed by the Board. The Committee 
is supported by an Enterprise Risk Management 
("ERM") team which provides advice on various 
risks and the appropriate governance framework 
and ensures that risks are identified, measured and 
managed in accordance with the Company's policies 
and risk objectives. The Committee holds meetings 
periodically where gap between two meetings does 
not exceed 210 days and that at least two meetings 
are held in a Financial Year. The risks faced by the 
Company and their minimization procedures are 
assessed periodically.
  According to Section 134(5)(e) of the Companies Act, 
2013, and Rules made thereunder, the term Internal 
Financial Control ("IFC") means the policies and 
procedures adopted by the Company for ensuring the 
orderly and efficient conduct of its business, including 
adherence to Company's policies, the safeguarding 
of its assets, the prevention and detection of frauds 
and errors, the accuracy and completeness of the 
accounting records, and the timely preparation of 
reliable financial information. The Company has a 
well-placed, proper and adequate internal financial 
control system which ensures that all assets are 
safeguarded and protected and that the transactions 
are authorised, recorded and reported correctly. 
The Company's internal financial control system 
also comprises due compliances with Company's 
policies and Standard Operating Procedures ("SOPs") and audit and compliance checks by the Statutory 
Auditors and the Internal Auditor. The Internal Auditors 
independently evaluate the adequacy of internal 
controls and concurrently audit the majority of the 
transactions in value terms. Independence of the 
audit and compliance is ensured by direct reporting of 
Internal Auditors to the Audit Committee of the Board. 
To further strengthen the compliance processes, 
the Company has a robust internal compliance 
management framework for assisting statutory 
compliances. Risk Management Policy is available on 
the Company's website at https://www.sudarshan.
com/investor/company-policies-sudarshan/
  Details of the Risk Management Committee are given 
in the Report on Corporate Governance.

guidelines and procedures that form part of internal 
control systems, which provide for checks and 
balances. The Company has maintained a proper and 
adequate system of internal controls. The system 
is designed to provide a reasonable degree of 
assurance regarding the effectiveness and efficiency 
of operations, the reliability of financial controls and 
compliance with applicable laws and regulations. 
The organisation is well structured and the policy 
guidelines are well documented with pre-defined 
authority where monetary decision is involved. 
Structured management information and reporting 
systems together with an exhaustive budgetary 
control process for all major operational activities 
form part of the overall control mechanism to ensure 
that requisite information related to all operations 
are reported and are available for control and review. 
The Company has established a well laid out policy to 
maintain the highest standards of environment, safety 
and health while maintaining operational integrity. 
This policy is strictly adhered to at all locations of the 
Company. The Company’s internal control systems are 
commensurate with the nature and size of its business 
operations. The Audit Committee of the Board of 
Directors regularly reviews the adequacy of internal 
control system.
  The Company, with a view to encourage independent 
approach, has appointed a team of qualified 
professionals in the form of Internal Auditors duly 
supported by the Finance Department who conduct 
operational and system audits in accordance with an 
audit plan approved by the Audit Committee. Internal 
Auditors as part of their assignment, evaluate and 
assess the adequacy and effectiveness of internal 
control measures and the compliance with policies, 
plans and statutory requirements. The internal audit 
reports are reviewed at Audit Committee Meetings 
and appropriate action on the recommendations is 
initiated by the Management.29.  RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT:

  Reporting on Audit Trail Feature:
  In terms of requirements prescribed by proviso to Rule 
3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, for the 
Financial Year commencing on or after the 1st day of 
April, 2023, every company that uses accounting 
software for maintaining its books of account should 
ensure that the accounting software used has an audit 
trail feature that cannot be disabled.
  Your Company has used accounting software for 
maintaining its books of account which has a feature 
of recording audit trail (edit log) facility and the same 
has operated throughout the year for all relevant 
transactions recorded in the software, except that 
audit trail feature is not enabled for changes, if any, 
made using certain administrative access rights 
to the application and underlying database, as 
described in note 58 to the financial statements. 
These administrative rights were restricted to limited 
users. Further, these administrative access rights at 
the application level have been revoked and audit 
trail feature at database is enabled subsequent 
to the year end. Further, no instance of audit trail 
feature being tampered with was noted in respect of 
such accounting software where the audit trail has 
been enabled.
  Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy:
  Your Company’s Whistle Blower Policy encourages 
Directors and employees and business associates 
to bring to the Company’s attention, instances of 
unethical behaviour, actual or suspected incidents 
of fraud or violation of the Code of Conduct that 
could adversely impact your Company’s operations, 
business performance and / or reputation. The 
Policy provides that the Company investigates such 
incidents, when reported, in an impartial manner 
and takes appropriate action to ensure that requisite 
standards of professional and ethical conduct are 
always upheld. It is your Company’s Policy to ensure 
that no employee is victimized or harassed for bringing 
such incidents to the attention of the Company. The 
practice of the Whistle Blower Policy is overseen 
by the Audit Committee and no employee has been 
denied access to the Committee.
  During the year under review, no complaint was 
received from a whistleblower.
  The vigil mechanism / whistle blower policy is available 
on the Company’s website at https://www.sudarshan.
com/investor/company-policies-sudarshan/

DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION POLICY
This Policy will regulate the process of dividend declaration 
and its pay-out by the Sudarshan Chemical Industries 
Limited ("the Company") in accordance with the provisions 
of Companies Act, 2013 read with the applicable Rules 
framed there under, as may be in force for the time being 
("Companies Act").
PREAMBLE
Dividend is the payment made by a Company to its 
shareholders, usually in the form of distribution of its 
Profits. The Profits earned by the Company can either be 
retained in business and used for acquisitions, expansion or 
diversification, or it can be distributed to the shareholder. 
The Company may choose to retain a part of its Profits for 
further expansion and modernization of the business and 
distribute the balance among its shareholders as dividend. 
This Policy aims to reconcile between all these needs.
The objective of this policy is to ensure a regular dividend 
income for the shareholders and long term capital 
appreciation for all stakeholders of the Company. The 
Company would ensure to strike the right balance between 
the quantum of dividend paid and amount of Profits retained 
in the business for various purposes. The Board of Directors 
will refer to the policy while declaring/ recommending 
dividends on behalf of the Company. Through this policy, 
the Company would endeavor to maintain a consistent 
approach to dividend pay- out keeping in mind the need to 
provide greater clarity on the dividend pay-out philosophy 
of the Company.
CATEGORY OF DIVIDENDS
The Companies Act provides for two forms of Dividend- 
Final & Interim. The Board of Directors shall have the power 
to recommend final dividend to the shareholders for their 
approval in the general meeting of the Company. The 
Board of Directors shall have the absolute power to declare 
interim dividend(s) during the financial year, as and when 
they consider it ft.
Factors to be considered while declaring 
Dividend
The decision regarding dividend pay-out is a crucial 
decision as it determines the amount of profit to be 
distributed among shareholders and amount of profit 
to be retained in business. The Board of Directors will 
endeavor to take a decision with an objective to enhance 
shareholders wealth and also meets the expectations of 
other stakeholders.
The Dividend pay-out decision depends upon certain 
financial parameters, external and internal factors.Financial Parameters
The following financial parameters will be considered while 
declaring or recommending dividend:
(i)  Operating cash flows ;
(ii)  Outstanding borrowings and obligations to creditors;
(iii)  Liquidity position;
(iv)  Stability of earnings;
(v)  Profit Before Tax and Profit After Tax;
(vi)  Profit growth targets for the current financial year, 
Profits for any previous financial year or years and 
market expectations;
(vii)  Availability of free reserves in conformity with the 
provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the 
relevant rules there under;
External Factors
State of Economy - in case of uncertain or recessionary 
economic and business conditions, the Board will endeavor 
to retain larger part of Profits to build up reserves to absorb 
future shocks.
Capital Markets - when the markets are favorable, dividend 
pay-out can be liberal. However, in case of unfavorable 
market conditions, Board may resort to a conservative 
dividend pay- out in order to conserve cash outflows.
Statutory Restrictions - The Board will keep in mind the 
restrictions imposed by Companies Act with regard to 
declaration of dividend.
Internal Factors
Apart from the various external factors aforementioned, 
the Board will take into account various internal factors 
while declaring Dividend, which inter alia will include-
i)  Profits earned during the year;
ii)  Present & future capital requirements of the 
existing businesses;
iii)  Brand / Business Acquisitions;
iv)  Expansion / Modernisation / Restructuring of 
existing businesses;
v)  Additional investments in subsidiaries / associates of 
the Company;
vi)  Any other factor as deemed ft by the Board.
Sudarshan Chemical Industries Limited

Annual Report 2025-26Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial Statements

=== page 35 ===
Circumstances in which Company may not 
declare / propose dividend
The Board of Directors will evaluate the financial 
parameters as well as the internal and external factors 
affecting / or which may adversely affect the performance 
of the Company in the short run before taking a decision 
as to not declare and / or propose dividend.
Dividend Range
The Company stands committed to deliver sustainable 
value to all its stakeholders. The Company will strive to 
distribute an optimal and appropriate level of the Profits 
earned by it in its business and investing activity, with 
the shareholders, in the form of dividend. As explained 
in the earlier part of this Policy, determining the dividend 
pay-out is dependent upon several factors, both internal 
to a business and external to it. Taking into consideration 
the aforementioned factors, the Board will endeavor to maintain an Annual Dividend pay-out in the range of 25% 
to 40% of Profits after tax (PAT) on standalone financials. 
However, the Board may amend the pay-out range, 
whenever considered appropriate by it, keeping in mind 
the aforesaid factors having a bearing on the dividend pay-
out decision.
Disclosure
This Policy will be disclosed in the annual report of the 
Company and on the website of the Company, as required 
under the Listing Regulations.
Policy review
The Board has the right to amend or modify this Policy 
in whole or in part, at any time without assigning any 
reason, whatsoever.
This Policy was approved by the Board of Directors at its

ANNEXURE V
ANNUAL REPORT ON CSR ACTIVITIES FOR THE FINANCIAL 
YEAR ENDED 31ST MARCH, 2026
BRIEF OUTLINE ON CSR POLICY OF THE 
COMPANY:
Introduction
Brief Outline on CSR Policy of the Company
Your Company’s aspiration to create sustainable and 
inclusive societal value is reflected through its Corporate 
Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives implemented under 
the aegis of SUDHA (Sudarshan’s Holistic Aspiration). 
The Company focuses on empowering disadvantaged 
and underserved communities residing in and around its 
manufacturing locations at Roha and Mahad, District Raigad, 
Maharashtra, through need-based and participatory 
development interventions. The CSR initiatives are aligned 
with the Company’s core philosophy of responsible growth 
and community partnership, with a strong emphasis on 
grassroots capacity building, environmental sustainability, 
and inclusive development.
Guided by Sudarshan’s Purpose — “Unleashing Vibrancy, 
Joy & Possibilities” — SUDHA strives to create meaningful 
and lasting social impact through initiatives in the areas 
of Livelihood, Health, Education, Women Empowerment, 
Environment, and Community Development. SUDHA is 
envisioned as a collaborative movement that strengthens 
the relationship between the Company and the communities 
in which it operates, while contributing towards improved 
quality of life, environmental stewardship, and sustainable 
community development.
To achieve the aforesaid goals, the Company adopted a 
series of CSR initiatives in Financial Year 2025-26 which 
involved programs, projects and activities to create a 
significant positive impact on identified stakeholders. All 
these programmes fall within the purview of Schedule VII 
of the provisions of Section 135 of the Companies Act, 
2013 and the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility 
Policy) Rules, 2014 (as amended from time to time).
SUDHA works towards sustainable growth of communities 
around its plants in Roha, Mahad and around its R&D Centre 
and Registered Office in Pune. In 2017, SUDHA started work 
on the Ideal Village Development Project. The work touches 
major areas such as women empowerment, education, 
health, environment, and community development.
SUDHA has outlined a systematic approach to address 
the ongoing issues in nearby areas. The organization 
collaborates with government authorities at various 
levels and works in coordination with Gram Panchayats 
of respective villages to initiate new activities. Apart from 
identifying the issues in respective villages and working 
with self-help groups to solve the problem, the Company also partners with nearby NGOs and corporates to ensure 
overall development of area through combined work.
Vision Mission and Objectives of SUDHA
Vision: Wholesome sustainable growth of each member of 
the community around Sudarshan Plants.
Mission:  R e a c h  o u t  t o  c o m m u n i t i e s  a n d  m a k e  l i v e s  
better by engaging in projects pertaining to Women 
Empowerment, Health, Education, Environment and 
Community Development.
Objectives:
• Serve Communities for a better future
• Create belongingness through sustainable 
inclusive growth
• Empower women for leadership
• Create groups to lead projects ahead
Framework of SUDHA
SUDHA has projects in 5 broad areas - Women 
Empowerment, Environment, Health, Community 
Development and Education.
Details of projects are as under:
1.  WOMEN EMPOWERMENT –
  The objective of the projects under this area is 
to empower underprivileged women in the local 
community by livelihood enhancement and vocational 
skill development. The purpose is to make women 
proficient enough through training to carry out the 
activities independently and earn a living. We have 
empowered 2,999 women. Projects undertaken so 
far include:
  A.  Paper Bag Project:  The Paper Bag Project stands 
as one of Sudarshan’s flagship CSR initiatives, 
successfully running for over nine years. This 
project empowers women by providing training 
in the production and marketing of eco-friendly 
paper bags of various sizes and strengths. These 
bags are crafted from recycled newspapers and 
can be produced at home, requiring no machinery 
or electricity, making it an accessible and 
sustainable source of income for rural women.
  B.  Sukushal Training Center : The Sukushal skill 
development initiative was started to run various 
skill-based training programs for rural youth, 
including stitching, beautician courses, and 
more. Initially, it focused on stitching, particularly for industry workers. Women have been trained 
in these skills, and as a result, they now earn 
an average of I5,000 to I15,000 per month. 
The Uniform Centre is a community-based 
skill development initiative aimed at enhancing 
employability among rural women and youth. It 
provides practical training in tailoring, garment 
production, and fashion design, promoting 
sustainable livelihoods and encouraging 
local entrepreneurship.
2.  ENVIRONMENT
  Under the Sudarshan CSR framework, SUDHA’s 
environmental initiatives focus on sustainable waste 
management and eco-friendly agriculture. Collectively, 
these efforts have benefitted 10,924 individuals, 
contributing to environmental conservation, soil health 
improvement, and sustainable rural development.
  Green Zone
  Aligned with Sudarshan CSR’s climate goals, Green 
Zone focuses on:
• Tree Plantation Drives  – Expanding green cover on 
common and marginal lands.
• Awareness Campaigns  – Educating communities 
on climate change and biodiversity.
• Wadi Model for Farmers  – Promoting horticulture-
based livelihoods by integrating fruit trees with 
agricultural crops to enhance farmers’ income and 
ecological resilience.
  A.  Water Conservation Project
   Key interventions in the Mahad region include 
Gabion structures, Nala plugging, farm 
bunding, CCT, and CNB. These have improved 
groundwater recharge and water availability, 
positively impacting 6,500+ individuals across 
8 villages.
 B.  Improved Agriculture
   Through the Horticulture Wadi Project and organic 
farming support, 1,200+ farmers (including 
150+ organic farmers) benefit from sustainable 
techniques, productivity enhancement, and 
eco-friendly practices, boosting income and 
livelihood security.
  C.  Waste Management
   Engaging 3,224+ families to create garbage-free 
villages. Wet waste is converted into compost 
using a decentralised Compost Planter (CP) 
Model, promoting community-led sustainable 
waste practices.3.  H E A LT H
  Under the Sudarshan CSR framework, SUDHA’s health 
initiatives focus on strengthening rural healthcare 
systems through government collaboration, frontline 
worker capacity building, and community awareness 
on mental health and menstrual hygiene. Collectively, 
these efforts have benefitted 12,202 individuals 
across various interventions.
• Collaborative Efforts with Government: Through 
partnerships with block-level rural hospitals and 
Primary Health Centres (PHCs), health camps and 
eye check-ups have benefitted 8,500+ community 
members, improving access to basic healthcare 
and strengthening local health infrastructure.
• Capacity Building of ASHA Workers:  Structured 
training programmes on leadership, communication, 
mental wellbeing, and community healthcare

empowering them to deliver better frontline

• Awareness on Community Mental Health: 
Mental health awareness sessions conducted 
for school students, ASHA workers, Community

• Awareness on Menstrual Hygiene:  A dedicated

4 .  E D U CAT I O N
  Under the Sudarshan CSR framework, SUDHA 
is committed to transforming rural education. In 
Financial Year 2025-26, the Sudha Sitara initiative 
has adopted 500 students to provide sustained 
educational support and mentorship.
 A.  Comprehensive Development of Rural 
Educational Institutes: ISO Certification for 
Schools & Anganwadis
   Education is fundamental to human development 
and national progress. SUDHA focuses on 
upgrading rural government schools by 
promoting digital learning, establishing science 
labs and libraries, and encouraging sports. The 
goal is to achieve global standards through 
ISO certification for schools and Anganwadis, 
ensuring quality education for rural children. 
To date, 44 Schools and 23 Anganwadis have 
been ISO certified, benefiting 17,335 students. 
These ongoing efforts are significantly improving 
educational quality in rural communities.

 B.  Collaboration with Expert Organizations for 
Promotion of Education Facilities
   SUDHA has partnered with expert organizations 
to provide quality education to underprivileged 
children, including those in urban slums, 
benefiting 2,105 students through supportive 
classes, Abhyasikas, and summer camps. Key 
collaborators include NGO – Seva Sahyog, Pune, 
supporting 405 children in Kothrud slum areas, 
and JMRE School, Roha, promoting education for 
1,700 students.
  C.  Sudha Sitara Scholarship Programme
   The Sudha Sitara Scholarship Programme is a 
flagship initiative under Sudarshan CSR, aimed 
at promoting higher education for meritorious 
students from economically weaker sections 
across Raigad district. To date, the programme 
has benefited 938 students through financial 
assistance and academic encouragement. The 
initiative places special emphasis on supporting 
girls and differently-abled students, fostering 
inclusive and equitable access to education. 
Through this programme, Sudarshan continues 
to invest in future-ready youth, empowering 
them to build sustainable careers and contribute 
positively to society.
  D.  Life Skill Development Programme
   The Life Skill Development Programme is 
designed to equip school and college students 
with essential personal, social, and professional 
competencies required for holistic development. 
Under this initiative, a comprehensive life skill 
training module was developed and implemented 
across 18 colleges, benefiting more than 2,000 
students. The programme focuses on enhancing 
communication skills, leadership, decision-
making, emotional resilience, confidence, and 
fostering a positive mindset among youth. 
Through interactive sessions and experiential 
learning approaches, the initiative has 
contributed towards building responsible, self-
aware, and future-ready young individuals.
5.  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
   Under the Sudarshan CSR framework, SUDHA 
is committed to fostering holistic community 
development through model village transformation, 
strengthening local governance, and ensuring 
social security for rural populations. To date, these 
initiatives have benefitted 27,058 individuals across 
project locations.   A.  Ideal Village Development Project & ISO 
Certification for Gram Panchayats
   To embody holistic development, SUDHA 
launched the Ideal Village Development Project 
across its operational locations, preserving the 
essence of rural India while fostering integrated 
development in personal, economic, social, and 
human spheres. Guided by the Adarsh Gram 
Yojana guidelines, the initiative aims to transform 
villages into model communities. The project has 
been implemented in multiple villages, impacting 
thousands of lives, with 15 Gram Panchayats 
successfully achieving ISO certification.
  B.  Transforming Village Governance: Capacity 
Building for Empowered Gram Panchayat 
Leadership
    SUDHA, under Sudarshan CSR, has initiated the 
Gram Panchayat Capacity-Building Programme 
to strengthen local self-governance and 
empower grassroots leadership. Implemented in 
collaboration with the Zilla Parishad and Block 
Panchayat authorities, the programme focuses 
on enhancing knowledge and capabilities of 
elected representatives in local governance, 
leadership development, participatory planning, 
and Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP) 
preparation and implementation.
    Programme Coverage:
• Gram Panchayat members trained across Roha 
and Mahad blocks -As part of the initiative, 
exposure visits to model villages are organized 
to provide practical learning opportunities. 
The programme has also motivated Gram 
Panchayats to participate in block and district-
level governance awards, promoting healthy 
competition, improved governance practices, 
and community participation.
  C.  Socially Secured Village
    SUDHA’s Socially Secured Village Initiative 
aims to strengthen community awareness and 
access to various government social security 
schemes at the village level, including health, 
insurance, pensions, education, and livelihood 
support. Eligible beneficiaries are identified 
and guided for enrolment through systematic 
community outreach. In collaboration with 
government departments, social security camps 
are organized to ensure easy access to scheme-
related services. Digital platforms are promoted 
to improve transparency and access. Through 
these efforts, the initiative has contributed 
to developing socially secure villages and 
enhancing social protection coverage. Composition of CSR Committee:

c.  A brief on types of customers
  Customer focus remains a core value and key business priority for Sudarshan. As a global provider of color solutions, 
the Company offers a diverse portfolio comprising organic and inorganic pigments, effect pigments, performance 
colorants, pearlescent pigments, and specialty chemicals. These products cater to a wide range of industries, 
including paints and coatings, plastics, printing inks, cosmetics, and other specialized applications, supporting 
customers with high-quality and reliable solutions for their end products.

Governance, leadership, and oversight
7.  Statement by director responsible for 
the business responsibility report, 
highlighting ESG related challenges, 
targets, and achievements (listed entity 
has flexibility regarding the placement 
of this disclosure)At Sudarshan Chemical Industries Limited, sustainability has been integrated 
into the way business decisions are evaluated, investments are prioritized, 
and operations are managed. During FY 2025–26, the Company continued 
to strengthen its ESG approach through alignment with frameworks such as 
SBTi, GRI, Responsible Care, UNGC, and the BRSR framework, supporting 
greater consistency, transparency, and accountability across sustainability 
governance and disclosures. The Company continued its participation in 
EcoVadis, CDP, and DJSI to support ESG benchmarking and strengthen 
sustainability disclosures.
Environmental performance remained key focus area during FY2025–
26, with ongoing efforts directed towards energy transition, emissions 
reduction, water stewardship, and waste management. Total energy 
consumption from renewable energy sources increased by 18.1%. 
Operational emissions intensity decreased by 1.3% compared to FY2024–
25, demonstrating progress towards carbon efficiency. Water optimization 
measures reduced withdrawal intensity by 1% per metric tons of production. 
In addition, sustained efforts in waste management resulted in a landfill 
diversion rate of 71.5%, significantly reducing waste sent to landfill.
During the year, we also undertook a Double Materiality Assessment 
(DMA) to reflect the evolving business structure, changing stakeholder 
expectations, and emerging ESG priorities, as One Sudarshan. Through 
CSR initiatives focused on education, healthcare, livelihood development, 
and community welfare, the Company positively impacted approximately 
68,985 beneficiaries during FY 2025–26.
As we advance as ONE Sudarshan, our operations, teams, and sustainability 
commitments are coming together into something more coherent and 
durable. That integration will shape how we strengthen our operations, 
progress on decarbonization, and meet the expectations of our customers, 
our markets, and the communities we operate in.

9.  Does the entity have a specified 
Committee of the Board/ Director 
responsible for decision making on 
sustainability related issues? (Yes / No). 
If yes, provide details.Yes. Sudarshan has established a structured governance framework for 
oversight and decision-making on sustainability-related matters at both 
the Board and management levels.
During the year, the Company constituted an ESG Committee at the Board 
level to strengthen strategic oversight of environmental, social, and 
governance priorities. The Committee reviews the Company’s ESG strategy, 
sustainability performance, material risks and opportunities, regulatory 
developments, and progress against key ESG objectives. It also provides 
guidance on integrating sustainability considerations into long-term 
business planning, stakeholder engagement, and governance practices.Disclosure QuestionsP

2P
3P
4P
5P

8P
9
At the management level, the ESG Steering Committee, chaired by the 
Managing Director, provides operational leadership and oversight to the 
Company’s sustainability agenda. It is responsible for reviewing ESG 
priorities, monitoring implementation of sustainability initiatives, assessing 
performance against targets, strengthening external ESG disclosures and 
ratings, and supporting the Board and its committees on sustainability-
related matters.
The ESG Steering Committee is supported by a cross-functional ESG 
Working Group comprising representatives from various business 
functions. The Working Group drives implementation of ESG initiatives 
across operations, tracks key performance indicators, identifies emerging 
ESG risks and opportunities, supports internal reporting processes, and 
recommends improvement actions and policy interventions. Periodic 
updates on ESG performance and progress are shared with the Steering 
Committee and senior leadership for review and guidance.

3.  Describe the processes in place to safely reclaim your products for reusing, recycling, and disposing at 
the end of life, for (a) Plastics (including packaging) (b) E-waste (c) Hazardous waste and (d) other waste.
Sr. 
No.Product Process to safely reclaim the product
i)Plastics (including packaging) The nature of contamination in packaging materials limits the possibility of 
recovery and reuse. Similarly, extracting pigments from end-use applications 
is not technologically viable at present. Therefore, Sudarshan does not carry 
out product or packaging reclamation at the end-of-life stage.
ii)E-Waste Sudarshan’s products do not contribute to the generation of electronic waste 
at the end of their lifecycle.
iii)Hazardous Waste Sudarshan’s products are incorporated into customers’ final products, which 
makes recovery or reclamation at the end-of-life stage technically impractical.

  Yes. Sudarshan’s operations are fully aligned with the applicable Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements,

of recycled plastic packaging materials and avoids the production of virgin plastic materials wherever possible. 
In addition, all plastic waste generated from operations is channeled for authorized recycling in accordance with

Yes/No (If yes, then give details of the mechanism in brief)
Permanent 
WorkersYes, IR Ninja and Works Committee as per The Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 have been established.
A monthly Works Committee meeting is held to facilitate open communication and direct 
dialogue between the worker representatives and management for collaborative resolution. 
On behalf of the workers, the recognized union committee members participate in the meeting. 
From the management of Sudarshan, the Site Head, IR (Industrial Relations) Head, and IR team 
are available in the meeting.
During these meetings, the union committee discuss grievances, issues, or suggestions raised 
by the workers. The forum serves as an important platform for addressing concerns, promoting 
mutual understanding, and working collaboratively towards resolving workplace matters in a 
constructive manner.
Other than 
Permanent 
WorkersYes.
IR Ninja
All contract and permanent workers have access through IR Ninja platform to raise grievances, 
confidentially and securely. The platform ensures timely acknowledgment, tracking, and 
resolution of issues.
Structured Redressal Process:
Grievances submitted through IR Ninja are reviewed by the internal team in every Tuesday, with 
resolutions provided within a defined timeframe, ensuring fairness and transparency.
Permanent 
EmployeesYes, Sudarshan has appointed an internal committee to address the employee grievances. The 
detailed grievance redressal mechanism is described below:
• HR Ninja & Suda Interconnect:  HR Ninja is an employee engagement initiative designed to 
address HR-related queries and concerns across Sudarshan. It serves as the primary point 
of contact for employees, helping monitor employee concerns and providing timely guidance 
or escalation wherever required. The initiative also tracks and analyses employee query 
trends through dedicated records. Suda Interconnect comprises quarterly location-level 
town hall meetings, where site leadership shares quarterly performance updates and future 
with employees.
• Suda Connect:  An annual Company-wide town hall conducted with all employees.
• Lean Daily Management Meetings
• Department-Level Meetings

a.  Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes/ No). If 
yes, the coverage such system?
  Yes, Sudarshan has implemented an Occupational Health & Safety Management System, with all its sites being 
certified under ISO 45001:2018.
b.  What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine basis 
by the entity?
  Sudarshan’s Risk Management System is structured to identify, assess, and manage health and safety hazards, 
along with credible risk scenarios associated with its operations. The system ensures that all personnel entering 
industrial sites are fit for duty and are not affected by fatigue or substances that may compromise safe working 
practices. Sudarshan remains committed to minimizing process safety incidents by actively promoting risk awareness 
among employees and workers. In addition, Sudarshan implements technical safeguards and nurtures a leadership-
driven culture that reinforces the importance of process safety. To further strengthen its approach, Sudarshan has 
collaborated with Risk Management Services to establish a comprehensive Process Safety Management (PSM) 
framework. The framework systematically identifies, evaluates, and mitigates operational health and safety risks. 
Furthermore, dedicated task forces have been formed to facilitate PSM element training for employees and workers 
at every stage of operations.
c.  Whether you have processes for workers to report the work-related hazards and to remove themselves from such 
risks. (Y/N)
  Yes, all employees and workers are actively involved in identifying task-related hazards through the Hazard 
Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) process. This process facilitates the identification and reporting of potential 
risks and supports the implementation of suitable control measures to effectively prevent and mitigate such risks.
d.  Do the employees/workers of the entity have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare services? (Yes/ No)
  Yes, Sudarshan ensures that all employees and workers are provided with comprehensive medical care to address 
any medical requirements, including emergency and routine healthcare needs.

12.  Describe the measures taken by the entity to ensure a safe and healthy work place.
  Sudarshan is strongly committed to ensuring employee safety and aspires to be an industry leader in occupational 
health and safety by working towards a workplace free from fatalities and serious injuries. Sudarshan’s ‘Zero Harm’ 
vision focuses on strengthening operational safety, nurturing a safety-oriented culture, enhancing workforce 
capabilities, implementing robust safety governance practices, and optimising asset performance.
  The Risk Management System adopted by Sudarshan systematically identifies, assesses, and manages health and 
safety hazards, along with credible risk scenarios associated with its operations. Sudarshan ensures that all personnel 
entering industrial sites are fit for duty and are not affected by fatigue or substances that may compromise safe 
working practices.
  Sudarshan actively works towards minimising process safety incidents by increasing awareness of potential risks 
among its workforce. To support this objective, Sudarshan has implemented technical safeguards and fostered a 
leadership-driven culture that places strong emphasis on process safety. In partnership with Expert Partner Risk 
Management Services, Sudarshan has also established a structured Process Safety Management (PSM) framework 
across the organisation.

5.  Describe the internal mechanisms in place to redress grievances related to human rights issues.
  Sudarshan’s Human Rights Policy  reflects its commitment to conducting business with respect for the dignity and 
rights of every individual, while fostering a workplace free from discrimination, harassment, and unfair treatment. 
The policy establishes a due diligence framework for identifying, assessing, mitigating, and managing human rights 
risks and impacts. The policy also adopts a zero-tolerance approach towards child labour, forced labour, trafficked 
labour, bonded labour, and any form of employment that is not based on free will and mutually agreed terms of 
employment. In addition, it incorporates mechanisms for monitoring, benchmarking, and reviewing objectives, while 
leveraging employee feedback to support continuous improvement through timely corrective actions. Further, the 
policy ensures access to remedy by addressing grievances in a transparent, fair, and timely manner. Business 
leaders and line managers are responsible for effective implementation of the policy, resolving grievances through 
established mechanisms, and actively supporting the grievance resolution process.
  Furthermore, Sudarshan’s IR Ninja and the Works Committee, have been constituted in accordance with the Industrial 
Disputes Act, 1947. Monthly Works Committee meetings are conducted to encourage open communication and direct 
interaction between worker representatives and management for the collaborative resolution of workplace matters. 
The meetings are attended by recognised union committee members representing the workers, along with the Site 
Head, IR (Industrial Relations) Head, and the IR team representing the management. During these discussions, the 
union committee presents grievances, concerns, and suggestions raised by workers. The forum plays a significant 
role in addressing workplace issues, strengthening mutual understanding, and fostering constructive collaboration 
towards effective resolution of concerns.
  For more details, refer to Page 76,  ESG Report FY 2024 -25

8.  Mechanisms to prevent adverse consequences to the complainant in discrimination and harassment cases.
  At Sudarshan, the workplace culture is founded on mutual trust and respect, ensuring an environment free from 
intimidation, harassment, exploitation, and oppression. Sudarshan remains committed to preventing, addressing, 
and rectifying any behaviour inconsistent with these values through the implementation of its Anti-Harassment 
Policy, supported by employee awareness programmes, mentoring, and guidance initiatives.
  To reinforce this commitment, the following mechanisms have been established:
• Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH): Sudarshan’s POSH Policy  strictly prohibits retaliation against individuals 
involved in reporting or investigating sexual harassment complaints. Any retaliatory action may lead to disciplinary 
measures, including termination of employment or legal action. The policy also mandates regular awareness and 
training programmes for employees and provides for the constitution of an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) 
to address reported cases in a prompt and impartial manner.
• Reporting Mechanism: A designated investigation committee reports directly to the Managing Director. Where 
required, the committee may seek support from departments not connected to the complaint to maintain objectivity 
and impartiality during the inquiry process.
• Grievances Against Internal Committee Members:  Any disciplinary or corrective measures resulting from inquiries 
conducted under the policy are considered final. The management remains committed to ensuring effective, timely, 
and comprehensive implementation of the policy.
• Internal Complaints Committee (ICC):  Constituted in accordance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at 
Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, the ICC is responsible for receiving, investigating, and 
resolving complaints related to sexual harassment. Committee members are trained to perform their responsibilities 
with sensitivity, confidentiality, and fairness.
9.  Do human rights requirements form part of your business agreements and contracts? (Yes/No)
  Yes, human rights requirements are incorporated into Sudarshan’s business agreements and contracts, under which 
suppliers, contractors, and business partners are expected to uphold this commitment by implementing policies and 
practices that promote and safeguard human rights.

8.  Does the entity have any project related to reducing Green House Gas emission? If yes, then provide details.
  Yes, Sudarshan Chemical Industries Limited is committed to achieving a 58.8% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions 
by FY2035, aligned with Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) targets. To support this commitment, the Company 
is implementing multiple emission reduction initiatives, including energy conservation measures and continuous 
monitoring to minimize flare emissions. Key interventions include CT fan temperature interlocking, modifications

5.  Does the entity have a framework/ policy on cyber security and risks related to data privacy? (Yes/No) If

  Yes, Sudarshan has established and implemented a comprehensive IT and Cybersecurity Policy aimed at 
safeguarding and effectively managing all IT-related resources used by employees, while ensuring compliance 
with legal, regulatory, and security requirements.
  As part of its broader policy framework, Sudarshan has also maintain a dedicated IT Management Policy that defines

standards of reliability and operational performance. Sudarshan also deploys robust, multi-layered physical and 
cybersecurity controls to safeguard sensitive information and critical systems.
